alt: Poster: Sensex 82,435.99 (-1.77%), Nifty 50 25,349.65 (-1.75%), Nifty Bank -3.17% on 23 Nov 2026; Nifty Metal -3.68%, Nifty IT +1.69%
text:
Indian benchmarks fell nearly 1.8% on Monday as banking and metal stocks led the decline.

• The Sensex closed at 82,435.99, down 1,483.72 points (1.77%), and the Nifty 50 at 25,349.65, down 450.95 points (1.75%), per closing reports from Kotak Neo, Univest and Marketcalls.
• Nifty Bank fell 3.17%, per the same reports.
• Nifty Metal fell 3.68% while Nifty IT rose 1.69%, per Kotak Neo and Univest sector data.
• Kotak Neo and Univest attribute the fall to selling in banking stocks and profit booking; Univest adds that indices were up more than 11% in November before today. NSE and BSE are closed on Tuesday 24 November.

Our view: after a strong run, a sharp one-day fall led by heavily weighted banks may reflect profit booking as much as any change in fundamentals, but one session is a small sample and the data cannot tell us which way the market goes next. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: do you read a single-day fall like this as routine consolidation after a rally, or does the breadth of the bank selling change how you view risk?
